articles.title: AI edtech startup Arivihan raises $10 mn from Accel, Prosus
articles.summary: Arivihan raises $10M Series A from Accel and Prosus as its Rs 51 annual plan drives 4 lakh+ paid students; funds to expand boards, AI and languages.
articles.body: BENGALURU: Indore-based edtech startup Arivihan has raised $10 million in a Series A round from existing investors Accel and Prosus Ventures. The funding comes as a shift to a Rs 51 annual entry plan has helped it draw more than 4 lakh paying students, co-founder and CEO Ritesh Singh Chandel told TOI.Arivihan previously charged an average of about Rs 3,000 a year for board exam preparation and had roughly 25,000 paying students last year. Chandel said about 4-4.5 lakh students have taken the new Rs 51 plan this year. The company offers higher-priced plans alongside it. “Our main focus was to get volume,” he said.The increase in subscribers does not necessarily mean a similar rise in revenue. Arivihan did not disclose its revenue or how many students have moved to more expensive plans. Chandel said 18% of subscriptions to the Rs 51 plan came through referrals.Founded in 2022, Arivihan began with Class 12 board exam preparation in Madhya Pradesh and has since expanded to other state boards and NEET. It says about 80% of its subscribers are from Tier 3 cities and rural areas. Chandel said the company built its courses and AI features for Hindi-speaking students first and is now testing Marathi. Students can also download lectures to watch when they have limited internet access.While Arivihan describes its platform as automated, its current classes combine human teachers and AI. Chandel said a live class can have as many as 5,000 students and one teacher, with AI answering individual questions and drawing on each student’s mistakes and practice history. The company plans to develop an AI tutor that can teach students one-on-one; that remains a future product.Chandel said about 5,000 students used Arivihan’s NEET preparation offering in its recent exam cycle and that three secured top-100 ranks. The company also cited internal data showing that 75% of students who completed five mock tests improved their marks by 25% over 30 days. It did not provide the size of that group or a comparison with students who did not use the platform.Arivihan plans to use the fresh capital to expand across more state boards and CBSE, improve its AI tools and language support, and build local distribution. articles.body: BENGALURU: Electric two-wheeler maker Simple Energy has raised Rs 1,750 crore ($180 million) in an all-equity Series C round, as the Bengaluru-based company looks to scale manufacturing, distribution and product development amid intensifying competition in the EV market.The round was led by the family office of Thyrocare founder Arokiaswamy Velumani, with participation from founder and CEO Suhas Rajkumar, co-founder and CFO Ankit Gupta, Bengaluru-based HNI Amit Mishra and the Haran Family Office. articles.title: The rise of agentic finance: Binance builds the infrastructure for autonomous trading
articles.summary: The era of artificial intelligence is fundamentally shifting from conversational interfaces to autonomous execution.
articles.body: The era of artificial intelligence is fundamentally shifting from conversational interfaces to autonomous execution. For the past few years, the primary utility of AI has been confined to answering complex questions, generating text, and summarising large datasets. Today, however, the technology is crossing a critical threshold into taking direct, independent action.When software acts autonomously, especially in the realm of finance, it needs to interact with capital markets in the exact same way human traders do. It requires live data, execution capabilities, and stringent security controls. As this new agentic economy rapidly expands, global financial infrastructure must evolve to accommodate AI as an active, independent market participant.The financial backing and market forecasts for this shift highlight a structural change rather than a temporary trend. Industry data shows that the global AI agents market is actively being funded, not merely forecast. According to MarketsandMarkets, the AI agents sector is projected to surge from approximately $7.8 billion in 2025 to over $52.6 billion by 2030, registering a compound annual growth rate of over 46 percent¹.This rapid expansion is echoed across enterprise software development. According to Gartner, 33 percent of enterprise software applications will include agentic AI capabilities by 2028, representing a massive increase from less than one percent in 2024².Establishing a financial capability layer for AIFor AI agents to be truly useful in the financial sector, they require secure, reliable, and standardised access to real-world market data and trading execution capabilities. Binance aims to address this exact need with the introduction of Binance Agent OS, a comprehensive developer platform built as part of its broader intelligence suite⁴. This operating system serves as a dedicated financial capability layer, allowing autonomous applications to discover and interact with crypto markets within a tightly controlled, auditable perimeter⁴.Binance Agent OS is designed to reduce fragmentation across agentic integrations⁴. Historically, developers had to stitch together bespoke, one-off connections to grant an AI model access to different financial tools⁴. Now, Binance Agent OS brings together various components, including Binance APIs, the Binance Wallet Agentic Hub, Binance x402, and the Binance Skill Hub, into a single, coherent ecosystem⁴. This consolidation formalises the company's commitment to building robust infrastructure for agentic crypto experiences and creates a foundation for expanding developer tools over time⁴.“Binance Agent OS addresses the fragmentation developers face when building agentic finance applications across crypto and traditional markets,” said Jeff Li, VP of Product at Binance. “It gives everyone from developers to quantitative traders the reliable data, low-latency infrastructure, and standardized interfaces they need to deploy AI-driven strategies,” he added.The power of the Model Context ProtocolAt the heart of this integration is the Model Context Protocol, commonly referred to as MCP⁴. MCP is an open standard that dictates how AI applications connect to external tools, data sources, and software services⁴. Rather than requiring developers to build custom integrations for every single AI model and financial function, MCP provides a universal connector⁴. This standard has already won the industry integration battle, having been adopted by major technology firms including OpenAI, Google, Microsoft, and AWS³.The adoption rate of this standard underscores its importance to the future of the internet.
